raw_response:
*Let me think this through as this farmer would...*

Aiya, another season. I've been doing this since I was thirty — 40 years now, same fields, mostly the same way. My back isn't what it was, but my sons help on the weekends, and my wife still goes to the field with me most days. The two boys work in the county town so we have some cash coming in, which helps when I need to buy fertilizer up front.

Let me think about the wheat first, since the wheat is already in the ground from last October — but I'll plan out what comes next.

**Wheat (winter, already planted last October on all 34.1 mu)**

I planted in mid-October like always, right after pulling up the maize. Used the "Jimai 22" variety — my nephew buys it from the agricultural supply shop in town, same as most people in our village. Saved some money that way compared to buying something fancy.

Before planting I spread about one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu (that's about 60 jin, or 30 kg — the 15-15-15 kind) and plowed it in. That's my base. My neighbor old Wang does the same, maybe a bit less. Now in spring I need to watch the wheat — if it looks yellow at the jointing stage (around late March, early April), I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu (20 jin, 10 kg). If it looks strong I'll do a bit less. I don't measure exactly, I go by the color of the leaves.

Irrigation: I already did the winter watering in November before the ground froze. This spring I'll water at returning-green (early March), then again at jointing, and once more at heading if the rain doesn't come. That's three waterings usually, four if it's a dry spring. The well water isn't free — the pump uses electricity and I have to pay by the meter. Each watering is maybe 30-40 yuan per mu. It adds up.

For weeds I'll spray once in spring — the village co-op sprays for several households together, costs a bit less that way. If aphids get bad near harvest I might spray once more but usually I don't.

Harvest in early June. I hire the combine — one of the younger guys in the village has one and charges by the mu. Then I have maybe 5-7 days to get the maize in the ground. Very tight.

**Maize (summer, will plant mid-June after wheat)**

Right after the combine finishes, I use the no-till seeder to plant maize straight into the wheat stubble. The agricultural station pushed this some years ago and it actually works — saves me from plowing, which I don't have time for anyway. I plant "Zhengdan 958" or whatever hybrid seed the shop has that year — must buy new every year, can't save hybrid seed, my neighbor tried once and the yield was terrible.

At planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (40 jin, 20 kg) with the seed — the seeder does both at once. Then when the maize gets to about knee-high (around late July), I side-dress urea, maybe 30-40 jin per mu (15-20 kg). That's when the plant really needs it. If there's no rain I water once before topdressing so the fertilizer goes in properly.

Maize doesn't need much irrigation here in a normal summer — usually one watering at tasseling if July is dry. Some years I don't water at all. The summer rain is usually enough.

I spray once for weeds right after planting, and sometimes once for corn borer in August if I see damage. I don't spray if I don't see pests — saving money matters.

Harvest late September. Again, hire the combine. The stover stays on the field, helps the next wheat.

**What I'm thinking about this year**

Fertilizer prices have been moving around. Last year urea was a bit cheaper than the year before. I'll buy what I can afford and not more. With 7 mouths to feed and the boys' wives and our grandchildren sometimes visiting, I can't spend everything on the field.

I don't change much year to year. My father farmed these same fields, mostly the same way. When something works, I keep doing it.
